name: HMB
lead: HMB (beta-hydroxy-beta-methylbutyrate) is a metabolite of leucine, sold as a calcium salt or free acid. It originated in studies of reducing muscle breakdown and has been used by lifters during hard training or calorie restriction.

Results depend heavily on who is studied. Meta-analyses suggest it helps preserve muscle in older adults and in clinical settings, while trials in trained young athletes mostly show little effect, consistent with a moderate rating.

paras: HMB is thought to reduce protein breakdown through effects on the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and to modestly support protein synthesis signalling and muscle cell repair. Human data for these mechanisms are less consistent than animal and cell work.

HMB is legal and has a good short-term safety record in trials. Reported side effects are minor, mostly gastrointestinal. Benefits in experienced trainees eating enough protein and training progressively are unconvincing, and quality of products varies.
